+    x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6 = row
+    
+    # Raw inputs (linear baseline terms)
+    f = [x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6]
+    
+    # Threshold features: binary indicators let linear model capture non-monotonic regions
+    f.append(0.0 if x4 <= -1 else 1.0)
+    f.append(0.0 if x4 > -1 and x4 <= 0 else 1.0)
+    f.append(0.0 if x4 > 0 and x4 <= 1 else 1.0)
+    f.append(0.0 if x4 > 1 else 1.0)
+    f.append(0.0 if x5 <= -1 else 1.0)
+    f.append(0.0 if x5 > -1 and x5 <= 0 else 1.0)
+    f.append(0.0 if x5 > 0 and x5 <= 1 else 1.0)
+    f.append(0.0 if x5 > 1 else 1.0)
+    
+    # Absolute value features: capture symmetric relationships that products miss
+    f.append(abs(x4))
+    f.append(abs(x5))
+    
+    # Log transform for skewed x3 (add epsilon to avoid log(0))
+    eps = 1e-6
+    f.append(math.log(x3 + eps))
+    
+    # Threshold bins on skewed x3 at strategic boundaries (percentiles)
+    f.append(1.0 if x3 > 0.5 else 0.0)
+    f.append(1.0 if x3 > 1.0 else 0.0)
+    f.append(1.0 if x3 > 2.0 else 0.0)
+    
+    # Quadrant indicators using copysign (safer than division)
+    f.append(math.copysign(1, x1 * x2))
+    f.append(math.copysign(1, x1 * x6))
+    
+    # Pairwise product interactions for XOR/quadrant patterns
+    f.append(x1 * x2)
+    f.append(x1 * x6)
+    f.append(x2 * x6)
+    
+    # Absolute value features (capture symmetry without sqrt)
+    f.append(abs(x3))
+    
+    return f
